subject: Discovery recap - migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Tina Park <tina.park@consultcorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap - migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Acme Health)

Alex / Tina - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard on the call and proposed next steps so we're all aligned. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points
- Vendor lock-in and rising token spend on OpenAI / Anthropic for chat and classification workloads.
- Latency spikes during peak hours impacting user experience for triage flows.
- Data residency and control concerns for PHI/PII (HIPAA discussion).
- Concern about integration effort: team wants minimal changes to existing OpenAI-style API calls.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Frontend app calls a backend service that proxies to OpenAI GPT-4 for chat / completion.
- Anthropic Claude used for safety-sensitive prompts and reranking.
- Token accounting and prompt templates live in a shared config service; some prompts use function-calling patterns.

Success criteria for migration
- API compatibility with minimal code changes (OpenAI-compatible endpoints or thin adapter).
- Equivalent safety profile (ability to run Claude-like safety checks or Redwood-provided reranker).
- Match or improve latency SLOs (<200ms p50 for short chat turns) and reduce cost by ~30-50% on target workloads.
- Support for data residency controls and audit logs for PHI.

Initial model shortlist (based on our discussion + workload profile)
- vicuna-13b-q4 (quantized) - good cost/latency tradeoff for chat.
- mpt-30b-instruct (trimmed) - strong instruction-following for special prompts.
- redwood-compat-xxx (hosted OpenAI-compat shim) - minimal code changes.

What Redwood will provide next
1) Attached: migration playbook (redwood-migration-playbook.pdf) - includes suggested rollout plan, test harness, and rollback criteria.
2) Compatibility matrix (we'll share a short spreadsheet mapping OpenAI/Anthropic API features to Redwood endpoints and recommended adapters).
3) Proposed pilot: 2-week pilot on a representative subset (support triage bot), with checkpoint metrics on latency, cost, and regression tests.

Next steps / timeline
- I'll share the compatibility matrix and a proposed pilot plan by tomorrow EOD (Fri 7/2).
- Technical deep-dive: schedule 60-90m session with Rishi (serving/runtime) and Aditya (security/integration) - proposed slots Mon/Tue next week.
- Please share any compliance/requirements docs (HIPAA checklist) - I've attached our standard migrations checklist and flagged areas we should cover.

Thanks - looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood-migration-playbook.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tina Park <tina.park@consultcorp.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap - migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Acme Health)

Thanks Marissa - useful recap. A few quick clarifications/questions from our security / infra side:

- Tokenization / detokenization: our prompt templates rely on OpenAI tokenization behavior in a few edge cases (truncated contexts). Can you confirm whether the recommended models preserve byte-level tokenization or whether Redwood supplies an adapter?
- Function calling: much of our orchestration depends on OpenAI-style function-calling. How does Redwood expose function calling (are there differences in signature or behavior)?
- HIPAA: we have a strict HITRUST/HIPAA checklist. Do you have existing customers in our space and any references or evidence (BAA process)?

Also - our timeline is tight: we're targeting a pilot by the end of July. Can Redwood commit to a 2-week pilot and provide any sample SLA/availability numbers for Dedicated or Private options?

I'm attaching a short requirements summary from our compliance team for your reference.

- Alex
Alex Johnson
Senior Product Manager, Acme Health
[Attachment: acme-requirements-hipaa.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Tina Park <tina.park@consultcorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap - migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Acme Health)

Alex - great questions. Quick answers up front, and we'll cover in the tech deep-dive: 

- Tokenization: Redwood provides a compatibility layer for OpenAI tokenization when needed; Rishi will bring specifics, but in short - for the edge cases we recommend running our tokenization adapter during the pilot so prompts behave identically.
- Function calling: we support OpenAI-style function calling via a shim endpoint. There are a couple of differences we'll document (mainly in how streaming partial function outputs are emitted); we'll include exact examples in the compatibility matrix.
- HIPAA / compliance: Redwood offers Private deployments and a standard BAA process. We have existing healthcare customers; Aditya will follow up with evidence and references.

Attachments: compatibility-matrix.xlsx (first draft) - includes field-by-field mapping and recommended adapter snippets.

Proposed technical deep-dive slots (please pick one):
- Mon 7/6 10:00-11:30 PDT
- Mon 7/6 15:00-16:30 PDT
- Tue 7/7 09:00-10:30 PDT

Pilot proposal: 2-week pilot targeting the triage bot (approx 50k tokens/day). We'll supply a pre-configured container for validation, and a short test harness to run regression checks.

Will loop Rishi + Aditya to pick the best slot and get you the BAA / references.

Best,
Marissa
[Attachment: compatibility-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap - migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Acme Health)

Marissa - quick internal note / action items before we surface to the customer: 

1) Action: I'll prepare a short tech deck covering tokenization adapter behavior, function-calling shim examples (including streaming pseudocode), and latency expectations per model.
   - Preliminary recommendation: run vicuna-13b-q4 for chat pilot with tokenization adapter enabled. If accuracy regressions appear, fall back to mpt-30b-instruct for those templates.
2) Action: Aditya - please pull the BAA + customer health references (we have two healthcare customers on Private deployment) and a short checklist of controls we can commit to for the pilot (encryption at rest, KMS key management, audit logs retention).
3) Timeline: aim to have the tech deck + references by Mon 7/6 morning so we can present in the 7/6 10:00 slot if the customer confirms.

I'll draft code snippets for both the shim and the thin adapter.

- Rishi
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
